AGENDA
  SPECIAL GLENDALE WATER & POWER COMMISSION MEETING
  VIA TELECONFERENCE ONLY
 Welcome to the meeting of the Special Glendale Water & Power Commission Meeting. Meetings
 are broadcast live on cable channel 6 (GTV6) and rebroadcast throughout the week. Call (818)
 548-4013 for program schedules. DVDs of the proceedings are available for purchase in the City
 Clerk’s Office. Meetings are also archived on the City Website for viewing anytime at
 https://www.glendaleca.gov/government/public-meeting-portal. If you have any question about
 matters on the agenda, or requests for assistance, please contact the Glendale Water & Power
 Administration Office at (818) 548-2107 during regular business hours.
  PLEASE TURN OFF CELLULAR PHONES WHILE INSIDE THE COUNCIL CHAMBER.
 In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) of 1990, auxiliary hearing aids, sign
 language translation, and Braille transcripts are available upon request. Assisted listening devices
 are available same-day upon request. At least 48 hours (or two business days) notice is required for
 requests regarding sign language translation and Braille transcription services. All documents related
 to open session items on this agenda that are received less than 72 hours prior to this meeting, and
 are public records, will be available for review in the Glendale Water & Power Administration Office,
 141 N. Glendale Ave., Suite 450, Glendale, CA 91206.
 Translation services are provided for meetings through the use of bilingual staff for speakers who
 wish to utilize the service as available. Speakers should state their request by contacting the City
 Clerk’s office at (818) 548-2090, at least 24 hours prior to the scheduled meeting. Please specify
 the language for which you require translation. The exclusive use of City provided interpreters is not
 required and persons are welcome to use their own interpreter or speak in their native language.
  JUNE 1, 2021 AT 4:00 PM

the LA County Health Department, the Special Glendale Water & Power Commission Meeting
meeting will be available to the public electronically.

Due to social distancing requirements, the public will not be able to attend the meeting. The public is
encouraged to watch and participate from the safety of their homes to practice social distancing.

The meeting can be viewed:

minutes_text:
MINUTES
  SPECIAL GLENDALE WATER & POWER COMMISSION

  VIA TELECONFERENCE

  Monday, June 01, 2021, 4:00 PM

Due to the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic, social distancing requirements, and health recommendations
from LA County Public Health Department, this meeting was conducted remotely. All GWP Commission
members and staff utilized video conferencing in order to virtually participate in the meeting.

1. ROLL CALL
  The meeting was called to order at 4:03 p.m.

  Present: President Flanigan, Commissioners Jazmadarian, Lall, Kedikian and Peterson.

2. GWP COMMISSION/ STAFF COMMENTS
  Commissioner Lall expressed her sentiments and condolences on the passing of Steve Zurn,
  former General Manager - GWP, and spoke of her experience working with Mr. Zurn. President
  Flanigan, and Commissioners Jazmadarian, Kedikian and Peterson concurred and echoed the
  same sentiments as Commissioner Lall. In addition, a brief tribute video was presented
  highlighting Mr. Zurn’s 34-year career working for the City.

3. REPORTS - INFORMATION
  a. GWP FY 2021-2022 Budget Presentation
  Mr. John Takhtalian, Interim General Manager for GWP, commented briefly on the
  proposed budget presentations and gave an overview of the GWP divisions and their
  responsibilities. He stated that the budget presentation is scheduled to go to City Council
  on June 8, 2021. Mr. Takhtalian complimented how GWP staff quickly adapted to the
  COVID situation by working remotely while continuing to provide exceptional customer
  service, including assisting customers who had trouble paying their bills and developing
  new bill assistance programs.

  Mr. Takhtalian introduced Mr. Craig Kuennen, Assistant General Manager - Business
  Services, who presented the proposed GWP FY 2021-2022 Budget and responded to the
  Commissioners’ questions.

  Commissioner Kedikian asked how GWP would be funding the proposed budget increase
  (11%). Mr. Craig Kuennen, Assistant General Manager - Business Services, responded by
  stating that the new Cost of Service Analysis (COSA) would cover a majority of the
  proposed budget, with the biggest amount being $27 million in the Power Management
  budget. Mr. Kuennen stated that he expects to receive the preliminary results of the new
  COSA from the consultant in approximately three to four weeks. President Flanigan
  commended the GWP staff on a job well done, especially during the pandemic.

  1
 4. ACTION ITEMS
  a. Proposed PBC Programs and Budget for FY 2021-22 and FY 2022-23
  Mr. Kuennen presented the Proposed PBC Programs and Budget for the next two years.
  Mr. Kuennen provided a brief background about the Public Benefits Background state law
  requirements and the four categories in which funds must be used:
   Cost-effective energy efficiency and conservation
   New investments in renewable energy resources
   Research, development and demonstration, and low-income electricity customers
  Mr. Kuennen provided details on the Proposed Budget and described the proposed
  programs within each of the required funding categories. He outlined the projected and
  proposed fund balance and high-level results. Mr. Kuennen and his staff responded to
  questions from the Commissioners regarding the PBC Programs.

  1. Motion Providing Recommendations to the City Manager and City Council to support the
  portfolio of the proposed PBC programs and budget.

  Moved by: President Flanigan
  Seconded by: Commissioner Kedikian

  Ayes:  President Lall, Commissioner Jazmadarian, Commissioner Kedikian,
  Commissioner Peterson, and President Flanigan
  Noes: n/a
  Absent: n/a

  Motion was passed unanimously.

  b. Proposed Low Carbon Fuel Standard Programs and Budget for FY 2021-22 and
  FY 2022-23
  Mr. Kuennen presented the Low Carbon Fuel Standard (LCFS) Programs and Budget for
  FY 2021-22 and FY 2022-23. He explained the regulatory background and purpose of the
  LCFS program and permitted use of the LCFS credits. Mr. Kuennen noted that the credits
  can be monetized and used to fund and promote the electrification of vehicles in the GWP
  service territory and will be used for the statewide point of sale electric vehicle rebate
  program.

  Mr. Kuennen provided the estimated fund balance on June 30, 2021, including cash and the
  value of unsold credits, of $6,426,651, and stated that the funds could be used solely for
  education and outreach, installation of public electric vehicle (EV) charging infrastructure,
  and charging station rebates and programs which promote EV adoption.

  Mr. Kuennen gave an overview of the various proposed programs that would be funded
  through the LCFS program. In addition, the Commissioners noted the benefits of the Solar
  Powered Mobile EV Charger program, which would prove to be beneficial in case of a
  catastrophic event, power outage, etc.

  1. Motion Providing Recommendations to the City Manager and City Council to
  to approve the portfolio of the Low Carbon Fuel Standard Credit Programs.

  Moved by: President Flanigan
  Seconded by: Commissioner Lall

  2
   Ayes: Commissioners Lall, Jazmadarian, Kedikian, Peterson, and President Flanigan
  Noes: n/a
  Absent: n/a

  Motion was passed unanimously.

5. ADJOURNMENT
  Motion to Adjourn:
  Moved by: Commissioner Kedikian
  Seconded by: Commissioner Jazmadarian
  Motion Passed.

The meeting was adjourned at 6:03 p.m.
